intro: If you're tired of the Bangsaen you usually picture — packed beaches and hotels lined up along the seafront road — Charn Residence sits in a much quieter corner of town · it's a small budget residence, a 4-storey building with around 20 rooms, on Bangsaen-Ang Sila Road right across from the road up Khao Sam Muk, a little past where most beach-goers gather · what guests talk about is the upper-floor rooms that look out over both the sea and the line of hills, the calm setting, the wide free parking, and the owner's grape vines planted around the building to match the name of the in-house restaurant, The Chardonnay · prices start at about ฿1,000/night · scored 7.9 from 6 reviews on Trip.com and 3.6 from 5 on Tripadvisor (ranked #3 of 7 specialty lodging properties in Saen Suk)

body.html: Charn Residence in a nutshell — who it's for — to put it the way you'd tell a friend, Charn Residence isn't a hotel selling luxury or a full set of facilities · it's a small budget residence, a 4-storey building with around 20 rooms, open since 2011, with two clear selling points: a quiet location at the foot of Khao Sam Muk and prices that start in the low thousands of baht · the people it suits best are couples or small groups of friends who want a cheap beach trip close to Bangkok, who aren't expecting a beachfront resort but want a clean, quiet place to sleep so they can head out to walk the beach, eat seafood, and drive up Khao Sam Muk in the evening · another group it fits well is people who drive themselves, because the wide free private parking is something many reviews agree on — it's easier to park here than in the beachfront zone, which gets jammed with cars on weekends · people coming for the Bangsaen Thailand Speed Festival or events near the circuit often pick this area too, since it's away from the crowds · on the other hand, if you're a big family wanting a pool, kids' activities, a lift, and round-the-clock service like a chain hotel, or you expect to cross the road straight into the water, this place may not be the right fit · simply put, Charn Residence suits people who come to "stay well for the money and get a quiet setting" more than people hunting for a full-service resort, and it's a stay where you need to set your expectations correctly before booking for it to land well

Location and getting around — Charn Residence is at no. 32 on Bangsaen-Ang Sila Road, in Saen Suk, Mueang Chon Buri, right across from the road up Khao Sam Muk · this is the part you need to be clear on before booking, because it isn't the main Bangsaen beach zone most people picture — it's the seafront stretch linking Bangsaen with Ang Sila, which is much quieter and has far less traffic than the main beachfront · the appeal of this spot is that you get calm, views of the sea and the Khao Sam Muk hills, and you're close to the real seafood · the standout nearby is Khao Sam Muk, with its troop of monkeys, the Chao Mae Sam Muk shrine, and a sea-view point almost directly across from the hotel — a few minutes on foot or by car up the hill · further on toward Ang Sila is the Ang Sila fish-pier market and the well-known seafront seafood restaurants, a few minutes' drive away · the main Bangsaen Beach, Nong Mon market and the Institute of Marine Science are about 5–15 min drive away · the honest caveat is that this location pretty much needs a car — several reviews say it's fairly hard to find a taxi or public transport because it's away from the main tourist spots, and it's quite a way to walk to the beach or into central Bangsaen (some reviews say about a 30-minute walk into central Bangsaen) · as for getting here from Bangkok, Bangsaen is one of the closest beaches, about 1.5 to 2 hours' drive depending on traffic, and around 1 hr 15 min from Suvarnabhumi Airport · in short, if you drive yourself this location is an advantage, but if you don't have a car, think it through carefully because getting around the area is harder than at the beachfront hotels

"Clean room, comfy bed, really quiet, and wide easy parking · in the morning you open the curtains to the sea and Khao Sam Muk — it really felt like a proper getaway, worth what we paid. But you do need your own car, everything's a long walk away."

Rooms and decor — Charn Residence has around 20 rooms across a 4-storey building, split mainly into Standard (a double or two single beds) and Deluxe, which are larger and mostly upper-floor rooms with the better views · rooms are about 26 sqm, decorated in a simple residence style — nothing flashy, but practical · in-room amenities are complete for a budget stay: air-conditioning, a fridge, minibar, flat-screen TV, kettle, tea and coffee, and a hot shower · some rooms have a balcony, and what guests mention most often is the upper-floor rooms that look out over both the sea and the line of the Khao Sam Muk hills — a view that's hard to find at this price, so if the view matters to you, ask for a higher-floor room when you book · most of the real reviews say the rooms are clean, the bed comfortable, plenty of pillows, and nice and quiet, well suited to an unhurried stay · but to be straight about it, some voices note that the rooms are an older style in keeping with a building open since 2011, the TV is fairly small and sometimes only has Thai channels, the walls in some rooms are fairly thin so you hear the room next door, and occasionally the in-room kit isn't complete — say a missing hairdryer or air-conditioning that doesn't get fully cold, which is the sort of thing you find in small budget stays at this price · another thing to know is that the building has no lift, so you take the stairs — if you get an upper-floor room with the good view, you trade that for carrying your own bags up · overall the rooms offer good value in a budget way, as long as you understand you're paying low-thousands-of-baht prices

Facilities and common areas — as a small residence, Charn Residence has no pool, gym or spa, and to be straight, anyone looking for those should consider somewhere else from the start · but what it does have, and does well in its own way, is wide free private parking — the thing reviews agree on most, and a genuine advantage in the Bangsaen area where parking is hard to find on weekends · there's a garden and greenery around the building, and what gives the place its character is that the owner has planted grape vines around the grounds to match the concept behind the restaurant's name, The Chardonnay, making the setting shady with a charm of its own · there's a bar and a seating area in the garden, good for sitting with a drink in the sea breeze in the evening · for security there's a key-card building access system, CCTV and fire equipment, which gives a degree of peace of mind · there's free Wi-Fi (mostly strong in the common areas and near the router, with weaker signal in some rooms the further out you go) · overall the common areas at Charn Residence are "just enough" — nothing luxurious, but the grape-vine garden, the wide parking and the quiet at the foot of the hill add up to a relaxed setting that fits the price

Food and the in-house restaurant — Charn Residence has an in-house restaurant called The Chardonnay, serving Thai food and offering breakfast (sometimes charged extra, sometimes included in the package — check when you book) with a view of the grape-vine garden · some reviews say there's a choice of both Thai and American breakfast, basic dishes that fill you up before heading out, not fancy but a fit for the size of the place · the upside of staying in this area is that you don't have to rely on the hotel for every meal, because all around you is the real seafood · a few minutes' drive gets you to the Ang Sila fish-pier market and the well-known seafront seafood restaurants with blue crab, shellfish, prawns and fresh fish at local prices · on the Bangsaen side there are seafront seafood spots, local specialties like hoi jor (crab rolls), and Nong Mon market selling khao lam, khanom jak and traditional Bangsaen treats to take home · so many people use Charn Residence as a base and head out to try the good spots around the area, which is the charm of staying in the Bangsaen-Ang Sila zone with its strong seafood culture · the one caveat on food is that the place itself is away from the dense restaurant cluster, so at night without a car it can be inconvenient to find food nearby — it's worth planning to pick something up to bring back

Service — service at Charn Residence is where the reviews are fairly mixed, and it has to be told straight · on the positive side, many reviews say the front-desk staff are helpful and can recommend things to do and places to eat around Bangsaen — being a small place, they look after guests attentively, like staying with someone you know · but on the side that has to be said plainly, some reviews note that some staff, or at certain times, aren't very smiley and have limited English, which left some foreign travellers feeling the service wasn't as warm as they'd hoped · there's also a room deposit of around 500 baht taken at check-in and returned at check-out, normal for this type of stay, but it's worth having cash ready and understanding it in advance · some reviews say daily housekeeping isn't as consistent as at a big hotel · overall the service is "adequate to good for the size and price" — not the main selling point, but not a big problem either for people who set their expectations as for a budget stay

What real reviews say (the good and the bad) — pulling together opinions from Trip.com, Tripadvisor, Booking.com and Expedia, the picture is fairly consistent for a budget stay · on the praise side: clean rooms and comfortable beds, a quiet setting good for relaxing, upper-floor rooms with sea and hill views, wide free easy parking, the charming grape-vine garden, good value for low-thousands-of-baht prices, and a location near the Ang Sila seafood · many sum it up as "not a big hotel, but worth the money" · on the caveat side: the most-mentioned point is that getting around is hard without a car — it's away from the main tourist spots, taxis are hard to come by, and it's quite a way to walk to the beach or into central Bangsaen · next is noise — not the traffic noise of the beach zone, but dogs barking and roosters crowing in the early morning, in keeping with the suburban hillside setting, plus the thin walls in some rooms that let you hear next door · then the building has no lift, the small TV is mostly Thai channels, the in-room kit is sometimes incomplete, staff at certain times aren't very smiley and have limited English, and there's a deposit at check-in · most of these gripes are things you can handle by understanding you're booking a budget hillside stay, not a beachfront resort, rather than flaws beyond what's acceptable

"Cheap, clean room, nice and quiet, lots of parking · the only downsides are some roosters and dogs early in the morning, and there's no lift — our room was upstairs so we had to lug the bags up ourselves. But for the sea view in the morning, it was worth it."

Price and value — prices start at about ฿1,000/night for a Standard room on weekdays, with the larger or better-view Deluxe rooms around ฿1,200–1,400 · on weekends, long holidays, and during events like the Bangsaen Thailand Speed Festival, prices climb and rooms fill up fast, since there are only around 20 of them · compared with other stays in the Bangsaen area, Charn Residence is among the cheapest — clearly cheaper than beachfront boutique hotels like Kalm Bangsaen or Bangsaen Heritage, which start from the low two-thousands and up · what you get back at this price is a clean room, a quiet hillside setting, wide parking, and the chance at a sea-view room on a low-thousands budget, which is hard to find in Bangsaen · what you trade is no pool, no lift, a location that needs a car, and small-stay service · for people who drive themselves and value money's worth and quiet over a full set of facilities, this price is good value · but measured on full-resort facilities or ease of getting around without a car, the same budget might do better at a beachfront stay or over on the Pattaya side · the score reflects this neatly: 7.9 from 6 reviews on Trip.com and 3.6 from 5 on Tripadvisor (ranked #3 of 7 specialty lodging properties in Saen Suk) — a budget stay that does its job well on a tight budget

What to know before you book — a few things help the stay go smoothly · one, you should have your own car, because the location is away from the main tourist spots, taxis are hard to find and everything's a long walk — the upside is the very wide free parking · two, if you want the view, ask for an upper-floor room (a higher-floor Deluxe) with the sea and Khao Sam Muk view, but understand the building has no lift so you take the stairs · three, if you're sensitive to morning noise, allow for dogs and roosters in the early morning in keeping with the suburban hillside setting, and pack earplugs · four, have cash ready for the room deposit of around 500 baht at check-in (returned at check-out) · five, check clearly whether the rate you book includes breakfast, since some rates charge extra · six, if you're coming during a long holiday or a festival, book ahead because rooms are few and fill up fast · seven, compare prices across platforms (Agoda, Booking, Trip.com) and try asking about booking direct via the Facebook page or by calling the hotel, since there are sometimes discounts for booking direct

The verdict — from all the real reviews, Charn Residence is the best fit for people who drive themselves and want a cheap, quiet beach stay close to Bangkok, with a shot at a sea-view room on a low-thousands budget · the hillside location at Khao Sam Muk across from the road up the hill, the wide free parking, the grape-vine garden, and the clean rooms make it a budget stay with a clear character and good value in the Bangsaen-Ang Sila area · if you're expecting a beachfront resort with a pool, a lift, full service, and easy travel without a car, this isn't the answer, and you should look at the beachfront boutique hotels in Bangsaen or a resort over on the Pattaya side instead · but if you're after a quiet, well-priced place for an easy drive-yourself beach trip focused on relaxing, eating seafood, and heading up Khao Sam Muk for the sea breeze — Charn Residence does that job well on an affordable budget, and it's why many guests say it was "worth what we paid"

faq.q: Where is Charn Residence · how close is it to Bangsaen Beach?
faq.a: Charn Residence is at no. 32 on Bangsaen-Ang Sila Road, across from the road up Khao Sam Muk, in Saen Suk, Mueang Chon Buri · near Khao Sam Muk, the Ang Sila fish-pier market, and the seafront seafood restaurants · the main Bangsaen Beach is about 5–10 min drive away · the location is away from the main tourist spots and everything's quite a walk, so a private car is recommended

faq.q: What's the starting price at Charn Residence · what rooms are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about ฿1,000/night for a Standard room on weekdays · larger or better-view Deluxe rooms run about ฿1,200–1,400 · there are around 20 rooms in a 4-storey building · over long holidays and festivals prices climb and rooms fill up fast, so book ahead and compare across platforms before booking

faq.q: Does Charn Residence have sea-view rooms?
faq.a: Yes · several upper-floor rooms look out over both the sea and the line of the Khao Sam Muk hills, which is what guests talk about and is hard to find on a low-thousands budget · if the view matters to you, ask for a higher-floor Deluxe room when you book · the trade-off is that the building has no lift, so you take the stairs

faq.q: Who is Charn Residence best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for people who drive themselves and want a cheap, quiet beach stay close to Bangkok, with a shot at a sea-view room on a low-thousands budget · good for an easy drive-yourself trip focused on relaxing, eating seafood, and heading up Khao Sam Muk · not a fit for people who want a resort with a pool, a lift, full service, or easy travel without a car

faq.q: Does Charn Residence have breakfast and a pool?
faq.a: There's an in-house restaurant called The Chardonnay serving Thai food and offering breakfast (extra on some rates, check when you book), with a choice of Thai or American · there's no pool, as it's a small residence · there's a grape-vine garden, a bar, wide free parking, and a key-card building access system

faq.q: Is there anything special to prepare for a stay at Charn Residence?
faq.a: You should have cash for the room deposit of around 500 baht at check-in (returned at check-out) · a private car is recommended because taxis are hard to find at this location · allow for dogs and roosters in the early morning in keeping with the suburban hillside setting, and pack earplugs · the building has no lift, so if you get an upper-floor room you carry your own bags up the stairs
